# American Wrestling Entertainment (AWF / AWE) — Universal Lore Bible

---

## 1. Corporate History & Rival Promotions

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **WWF → WWE** | **AWF → AWE** (**American Wrestling Federation** → **American Wrestling Entertainment**) | Founded and controlled by ruthless billionaire CEO **Chairman Victor Cross**. Rebranded from **AWF** to **AWE** in May 2002. |
| **World Wildlife Fund (WWF)** | **The Animal Welfare Fund (AWF)** | London-based international wildlife conservation fund. Successfully sued Chairman Victor Cross in the English High Court in 2002 for violating a 1994 co-existence agreement over the AWF initials, forcing the transition to **AWE**. |
| **"Get the F Out" Campaign** | **"We're getting the 'F' out!"** | Chairman Victor Cross's defiant May 2002 marketing slogan used to rebrand the **AWF** into **AWE** following the London lawsuit. |
| **WCW (World Championship Wrestling)** | **GCW (Global Championship Wrestling)** | Atlanta-based rival promotion that waged the 1990s ratings war against the AWF before being purchased by Victor Cross in March 2001, triggering the 2001 Invasion angle and the 2002 **AWE Brand Extension** draft. |
| **ECW (Extreme Championship Wrestling)** | **HCW (Hardcore Championship Wrestling)** | Philadelphia-based extreme wrestling promotion run by **Carter "The Fox" Finnley** out of the legendary **South Philly Bingo Hall** (the **Viking Hall / HCW Arena** at Swanson & Ritner). Acquired by AWE after its 2001 bankruptcy and revived in 2006 as AWE's third brand. |
| **"This Is Extreme!"** *(Harry Slash & The Slashtones — ECW Theme)* | ***"This Is Hardcore!"*** *(The South Street Slashtones — HCW Theme)* | The unmistakable, gritty drop-D industrial guitar riff, driving cowbell beat, and gravelly voiceover (*"THIS! IS! HARDCORE!"*) that opened every late-night HCW broadcast and sent the faithful chanting *"H-C-W! H-C-W!"* whenever a table was set on fire or a Singapore cane came out from under the ring. |
| **Titan Towers (Stamford, CT)** | **Titan Plaza (Stamford, CT)** | Corporate headquarters of American Wrestling Entertainment. |
| **TitanTron** | **TitanTron** | The colossal high-definition entrance stage video screen above the ramp. |

---

## 2. Corporate Terminology

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **WWE Superstar** | **AWE Titan** | Strictly enforced corporate branding for male professional wrestlers on the AWE roster. |
| **WWE Diva / Women's Division** | **AWE Icon** | Corporate branding for the female roster (transitioning from the 2000s "Icon" era to the mid-2010s Women's Evolution). |
| **WWE Universe** | **The AWE Legion** | Official marketing term for AWE's global fanbase. |
| **Ringside Collectible Chair** | **AWE Ringsider Folding Chair** | Heavy, padded black commemorative steel folding chairs zip-tied together in the front rows of live broadcasts and Pay-Per-Views, which Ringsider ticket holders take home after the main event. |

---

## 3. Complete Television Broadcast Lineup (Historical & Modern)

### Flagship Weekly "A-Shows"

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Monday Night RAW** (1993–present) | **AWE Monday Night WAR** (stylized in the late-1990s Attitude Era as *WAR IS WAR*) | **Mondays (Live, 8:00/9:00 PM EST)** | Rachel's ultimate hyperfixation in /rachel (attending the November 20, 2006 broadcast live at the Rose City Center in Portland, OR in Book 16). ## 4. The Complete Annual Pay-Per-View (PPV) Calendar

AWE produces twelve monthly Sunday night Pay-Per-View extravaganzas each year, anchored by **"The Big Four"** (*The Iron Gauntlet*, *The Pinnacle*, *Summer Siege*, and *No Quarter*):

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **January** | **Royal Rumble** *(Big Four)* | **The Iron Gauntlet** | Kickoff to the Road to *The Pinnacle*. Headlined by the **30-Man Iron Gauntlet Match**, where a new Titan enters every 90–120 seconds; elimination only occurs when thrown over the top rope and *both feet* touch the arena floor, with the winner earning a World Championship main-event match at *The Pinnacle*. |
| **February** | **No Way Out** / **Elimination Chamber** | **No Escape** | Final stop before *The Pinnacle*. Features the **Iron Dome Match** (*Elimination Chamber*)—a 16-foot-high, 10-ton circular steel-and-chain prison with four polycarbonate corner pods. |
| **March / Early April** | **WrestleMania** *(Big Four)* | **The Pinnacle** | *"The Grandest Stage of Them All."* AWE's flagship annual stadium supershow and cultural phenomenon. |
| **Late April** | **Backlash** | **Fallout** | Features the immediate championship rematches and blood feuds spinning out of *The Pinnacle*. |
| **May** | **Judgment Day** / **Over the Limit** / **Payback** | **Day of Reckoning** | Late-spring grudge-match Pay-Per-View. |
| **June** | **King of the Ring** (1993–2002) / **Bad Blood** (2003–2004) / **One Night Stand** (2005–2008) / **Money in the Bank** (2010–present) | **Crown of the Ring** / **Bad Bloodline** / **One Night Only** / **Contract in the Vault** | Historic June PPV slot; in the 2010s era (/aubrie), features the multi-man **Contract in the Vault Ladder Match** for a briefcase guaranteeing a World Title match anywhere, anytime within one year. |
| **July** | **Vengeance** / **The Great American Bash** / **Battleground** | **Vendetta** / **The Liberty Bash** / **Battlefront** | Mid-summer championship Pay-Per-View building toward *Summer Siege*. |
| **August** | **SummerSlam** *(Big Four)* | **Summer Siege** | *"The Biggest Event of the Summer."* AWE's second-largest annual supershow, held each August in a major coastal or metropolitan arena. |
| **September** | **Unforgiven** (1998–2008) / **Night of Champions** (2008–2015) | **Unrelenting** / **Night of Gold** | Early autumn PPV; under the *Night of Gold* banner (2008–2015), every single active championship in the AWE is defended on the same card. |
| **October** | **No Mercy** (1999–2008) / **Taboo Tuesday & Cyber Sunday** (2004–2008) / **Hell in a Cell** (2009–present) | **Zero Mercy** / **Cyber Clash** / **The Iron Cell** | October autumn classic; features the **Iron Cell** (*Hell in a Cell*) 20-foot roofed steel cage structure. |
| **November** | **Survivor Series** *(Big Four)* | **No Quarter** | **The Annual Thanksgiving Week Tradition.** AWE's historic November "Big Four" Pay-Per-View, held on the Sunday before (or of) Thanksgiving week. Famous for traditional **5-on-5 No Quarter Elimination Tag Team Matches** and career-defining stipulation bouts. In /rachel (Books 16–17), Michael, Rachel, Jessica, and Kristin sit in front-row Ringsider seats for **AWE *No Quarter* 2006** at The Emerald Coliseum in Seattle, WA on Sunday, November 26, 2006. In /aubrie, *No Quarter* is a centerpiece of the suite's annual Thanksgiving Sanctuary tradition at Daniel and Laura Brooks' home in Christiansburg. |
| **December** | **Armageddon** (1999–2008) / **TLC: Tables, Ladders & Chairs** (2009–present) | **Doomsday** / **TLS: Tables, Ladders & Steel** | Year-end December blow-off Pay-Per-View featuring multi-man demolition matches with tables, ladders, and steel folding chairs. |

nodes.name: Katie Prairie
nodes.summary: Born April 8, 1985 in Virginia Beach, Virginia alongside her fraternal twin brother Nathaniel ('Nate') Prairie, Katie is an autistic wheelchair user whose lifelong bond with Nate anchors Katie & Nathaniel from their childhood afternoon cartoon sanctuary onward.
nodes.subtitle: Co-Protagonist • Fraternal Twin Sister

nodes.name: Nathaniel "Nate" Prairie
nodes.summary: Born April 8, 1985 in Virginia Beach, Virginia, Nathaniel ('Nate') Prairie is Katie's autistic fraternal twin brother, narrator, and inseparable safe person—sharing cartoon passwords, transit routes, and stepless sanctuaries side by side.
nodes.subtitle: POV Narrator & Co-Protagonist • Fraternal Twin Brother

nodes.name: Ryan O'Connell
nodes.summary: Born in 1964 and raised in Blacksburg, Virginia alongside his sisters Cassidy and Holly and twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright, Ryan O'Connell is the co-lead vocalist, electric guitarist, and primary lyricist of The Stardust Engine. An autistic T10 paraplegic manual wheelchair user whose rear push-handles serve as Cassidy's steady walking support, Ryan anchors both The Stardust Engine and Escape Velocity: Ad Astra.
nodes.subtitle: Co-Lead Vocalist, Lead Guitarist & Lyricist — The Stardust Engine

nodes.name: Cassidy O'Connell
nodes.summary: Born in 1967 in Blacksburg, Virginia, Cassidy O'Connell is the co-lead vocalist, analog synthesizer architect, and composer of The Stardust Engine's Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ and 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra).' Living with cerebral palsy and autism, Cassidy walks using the rear push-handles on her brother Ryan's manual wheelchair.
nodes.subtitle: Co-Lead Vocalist, Analog Synthesizer Architect & Composer — The Stardust Engine

nodes.name: Holly O'Connell, J.D., CFA
nodes.summary: Born in 1969 as the youngest O'Connell sibling on Progress Street NE in Blacksburg, Holly O'Connell serves as The Stardust Engine's fiercely protective day-to-day manager, general counsel, Class A CDL co-driver, and in-universe founder of Engine Room Records, LLC.
nodes.subtitle: Band Manager, General Counsel & In-Universe Founder of Engine Room Records, LLC

nodes.name: Evan Wright
nodes.summary: Born October 31, 1967, Evan Wright is Tyler Wright's identical twin brother and maternal cousin to Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell—anchoring The Stardust Engine's low-end synth-bass architecture and Class A touring logistics from Blacksburg to Caelum-IV.
nodes.subtitle: Bassist, Sub-Bass Synth Architect & Systems Engineer — The Stardust Engine

nodes.name: Tyler Wright
nodes.summary: Born October 31, 1967, Tyler Wright is Evan Wright's identical twin brother and maternal cousin to the O'Connell siblings—driving both The Stardust Engine's acoustic/electronic rhythm section and their custom accessible touring fleet.
nodes.subtitle: Drummer, Percussionist & Lead Fleet Driver — The Stardust Engine

nodes.name: Claire Manning
nodes.summary: Older sister of Rhys Manning in Fractured Prisms. Born into the British-American Manning Family Orchestra in Romford, East London, Claire is autistic and uses a manual wheelchair due to lifelong cerebral palsy, weaving Cousin Gwen's salvaged wooden concert flute and soaring vocals across Carnaby Street and 1883.
nodes.subtitle: Lead Vocalist & Concert Flutist — Fractured Prisms

nodes.name: Rhys Manning
nodes.summary: Younger brother and lifelong safe person to Claire Manning in Fractured Prisms, engineering their analog synthesizer rock operas in Williamsport, Maryland and restoring Downtown Hagerstown's 1914 Colonial Theatre into a stepless performance sanctuary.
nodes.subtitle: Synthesizer Architect, Multi-Instrumentalist & Safe Person — Fractured Prisms

nodes.name: The Stardust Engine
nodes.summary: The founding five-member family unit behind Engine Room Records. Forged at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in 1985–1986 by siblings Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell and identical twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright, The Stardust Engine blends soaring 1980s stadium synth-rock with Cassidy's zero-gravity Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™.
nodes.subtitle: 80s Synth-Pop / Arena Rock / 80s Cosmic Pop

nodes.name: Fractured Prisms
nodes.summary: Formed by surviving British-American siblings Claire Manning (older sister; autistic and living with lifelong cerebral palsy, uses a manual wheelchair) and Rhys Manning (younger brother; neurotypical synthesizer architect and lifelong safe person) after the winter 1981 M6 Shap Fell motorway pileup claimed the other four members of the Manning Family Orchestra. Fleeing to their father's vacant 1960s ranch house in Williamsport, Maryland, they built "The Fragile Fortress"—weaving the salvaged instruments of their lost family (including Cousin Gwen's wooden concert flute) into towering 1980s analog synthesizer rock operas set inside the gaslamp-lit 1883 Victorian sanctuary of The Hollow Square.
nodes.subtitle: 80s Progressive Art-Rock / British Synth-Pop / Victorian Rock Opera

nodes.name: The Paper Wall
nodes.summary: Engine Room Records' first outside signing (2001). Formed by Julian Croft ("Leo") and Maya Sterling ("Olivia") alongside Julian's sisters and cousins, The Paper Wall transforms survival, disability rights, and found-family sanctuary into multi-volume literary rock operas.
nodes.subtitle: Literary Rock Opera / Alternative & Industrial Rock

nodes.name: The Arctic Symphony Project
nodes.summary: Born on a freezing December night in 1996 when the Rowlands and Harrison siblings turned their Williamsburg living room into an emergency broadcast studio to guide abducted 14-year-old Julian ("Julep") home across the Appalachian Mountains with "Upon This Winter's Night."
nodes.subtitle: Holiday Symphonic Rock / Neoclassical Metal / Rock Opera

nodes.name: Crimson Node

nodes.name: Mana Canvas

nodes.subtitle: Symphonic Fantasy Rock / 16-Bit Chiptune Prog / JRPG Soundtrack

nodes.name: Firelight
nodes.summary: The official 1980s motion picture soundtrack ensemble behind The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel—Michael P. Ragsdale's love letter to 1980s fantasy-adventure cinema. Anchored by its flagship main theme "A Sister's Love" (heavily inspired by classic 1984 widescreen fantasy cinema synth-pop themes), Firelight fuses shimmering 1980s analog synth-pop arpeggios and soaring melodic hooks with widescreen fantasy orchestration.
